points.t: A child (often 3–10 years) with palpable purpura on the legs and buttocks after a cold or sore throat, with sore joints or tummy pain.
IgA-containing immune complexes in small vessels of the skin, gut, joints and kidneys.
Exclude sepsis; BP and urine dipstick; FBC and clotting if unsure; simple analgesia; urine and BP monitoring for 6–12 months.
Meningococcal sepsis, leukaemia or ITP (check platelets), intussusception, nephritis.

points: **Palpable purpura** (100%, required): symmetrical on the **buttocks, legs, ankles and extensor arms**, ± urticarial and bullous/necrotic lesions; scrotal oedema; oedema of the scalp/face in toddlers.
**Arthralgia/arthritis** (~75%): knees and ankles, transient and non-erosive.
Rare: orchitis/testicular torsion mimic, CNS involvement, pulmonary haemorrhage.
**FBC + film (platelets normal — excludes ITP/leukaemia)**, clotting, U&E/creatinine, albumin, CRP; ASO ± throat swab; IgA (raised in ~50%; not diagnostic).
only if atypical (adults, uncertain diagnosis): LCV with **perivascular IgA and C3 on DIF**. Renal biopsy if significant proteinuria or impaired function.

items.t: Child unwell, febrile or with spreading non-blanching rash: treat as **meningococcal disease** until proven otherwise.
Severe abdominal pain or blood in stool: possible **intussusception**, same-day paediatric review.
Proteinuria, haematuria or high BP: paediatric nephrology advice; keep checking urine for 6–12 months.

pearls.t: "**HSP = purpura with a NORMAL platelet count.**" If platelets are low, it is not HSP.
Give the family a **urine dipstick plan** and a written list of red flags (abdominal pain, blood in urine/stools, swollen testicles, headache, reduced urine output).
The rash can recur with activity/standing — reassure.
